question.problem: If $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=4$ for some $x$, then find the value of $\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cot}⁡(x+2\pi )-3.$
question.worked_solution:
The period of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ is $\pi .$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

$$
\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\operatorname{cot}⁡(x+n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=2$ into the right-hand-side of the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\operatorname{cot}⁡(x+(2)\cdot \pi )=\operatorname{cot}⁡(x+2\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=4,$ then $\operatorname{cot}⁡(x+2\pi )=4.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cot}⁡(x+2\pi )-3 & =\frac{1}{2}(4)-3 \\  & =2-3 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$
